text:
Alex: Quick question for runtime folks — thinking about how we merge prefix cached state when a prefix is demoted on Node A and Node B concurrently prefetches the same prefix. Today demote is a best-effort tombstone + local eviction and we see rare stale reads during handoff. Any quick takes? (5m)

Jamie: Do you have a concrete repro or is this based on metrics/alerts?

Alex: Saw a customer complaint + correlating telemetry: small % of reads return older embeddings for ~200ms window after handoff. I can share traces.

Maria: Two quick failure modes I remember: (1) demote evicts locally but doesn’t publish a global epoch/tombstone reliably, so a prefetch from B wins and writes a new cache entry derived from stale state, and (2) B serves from its warm snapshot then later applies newer writes. Both lead to transient inconsistency.

Devon: Right. We tried the tombstone pubsub approach last year but it got flaky under load. The pubsub misses + retry window is the culprit.

Sylvia: Idea: move from best-effort tombstones -> compact epoch tokens attached to prefix descriptors. When demote happens, bump epoch and publish a small 64-bit token in the metadata store (consistent store). Readers compare token, if mismatch they force revalidate.

Jamie: That adds a read-check on cache gets though. Latency impact?

Maria: We can optimize: only check token on cache miss or on load-from-prefill path. For hot-path gets served from in-memory KV, skip token check. So code path:

```
GET(prefix):
  if in_mem_hit: return value
  else:
    token = mtstore.get_token(prefix)  // cheap read, cached locally with TTL
    if token != cached_token: refresh_from_source()
    else serve_cached_value
```

Devon: mtstore reads still add extra ops on cold reads. But cold reads are already heavy (rebuild embeddings etc). A single token read is cheap compared to model inference.

Alex: Two followups: (A) how do we ensure epoch writes are linearizable for prefix moves? (B) how to handle long-tail clients that don't revalidate quickly (stale KV readers)?

Sylvia: For (A) write epoch bump as compare-and-set against descriptor version in the control plane (we already have descriptor CAS for shard moves). For (B) we can attach epoch token to prefill/async write operations — writers include token they saw; if server sees older token it should either reject or force a tombstone-and-rebuild flow.

Jamie: That means we need API surface changes: writers must call Prefill.Put(prefix, token) and Put returns conflict if token mismatches. Is that acceptable?

Maria: Seems fine — existing prefill path already is async and retries. We'll need to harden failure semantics: on conflict, prefill should re-fetch the descriptor and restart.

Devon: Also need metrics: prefix_epoch_mismatch_count, prefix_rebuild_latency, stale_read_rate. Canary plan: enable token-checking in canary region for 48h and compare stale_read_rate drop.

Alex: Good. Concerns about control-plane availability — if mtstore is partitioned we'll have trouble bumping token on demote. Do we need fallback?

Sylvia: Fallback: if we can't write token, fall back to broad lease-based eviction (short window) and error budget. But this should be rare. Another fallback is to mark prefix as "soft-demote" and block prefill on other nodes till token sync completes.

Jamie: Not a fan of blocking prefill — could cause cold-start spikes. Prefer soft fallback + increase sampling to detect regressions.

Maria: Action items I can take: 1) Spike to implement epoch token in mtstore prototype (2d). 2) Add prefill conflict path + tests (3d). 3) Add unit + integration tests for concurrent demote+prefill (branch).

Alex: Sounds good. I'll open a short RFC and link here: <https://go/repo/rfc/prefix-epoch-reconcile|RFC draft>. Let's also add the metrics and a canary checklist.

infra-bot: New job created: infra/canaries/prefix-epoch-check (owner: Maria).

Devon: FYI I'll pair with Maria on the integration tests — need to simulate partition + delayed descriptor propagation.

Sylvia: One more thought: tombstones still useful for immediate eviction of hot in-mem data. Epoch token covers correctness, tombstone covers immediate memory reclaim. Keep both.

Alex: Agreement: epoch token + tombstone hybrid. Maria to spike, Devon to help tests, Jamie to review perf implications, Sylvia for control-plane failure modes. We'll sync after spike. Thanks :thumbsup:
